Looking at panel a, we see a Western blot analysis of HeLa cells under different conditions: shControl, shFMR1, and shFXR1. For each condition, there are three lanes: T (Total), C (Cytoplasm), and N (Nucleoplasm).

We are asked which cells contain ADAR2 within the cytoplasm — that is, in the “C” lane for ADAR2.

Looking at the ADAR2 row:

- In shControl: C lane shows a band → ADAR2 is present in cytoplasm.
- In shFMR1: C lane shows a band → ADAR2 is present in cytoplasm.
- In shFXR1: C lane shows a band → ADAR2 is present in cytoplasm.

So ADAR2 is detected in the cytoplasm in all three conditions: shControl, shFMR1, and shFXR1.

The question asks: “which of the following cells contain ADAR2 within the cytoplasm?” and gives options including individual shRNA conditions and “none of the above”.

Since ADAR2 is present in the cytoplasm in shControl (as well as others), option (B) shControl is correct — it is one of the cell types that contains ADAR2 in the cytoplasm.

Note: The question does not say “only” or “exclusively”, so if any of the listed options is true, it’s acceptable. Since shControl clearly has ADAR2 in cytoplasm, (B) is correct.

[ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
